general: Fiduciary lien (Lei 9.514/97): a contract with a registered lien can only be terminated through the special procedure of arts. 26 and 27; the preliminary objection that an ordinary rescission action is the wrong procedure is routinely missing from the defence.

Delay in a lot development is not automatic: the 48-month term of Lei 6.766/79 is regulatory and the works schedule is an estimate subject to public approvals and registrations; the defence rarely says so.
Buyer inertia: a buyer who never asked for a building permit, a site visit or a project approval weakens presumed lost profits and triggers the duty to mitigate; seldom used.
Association fees in gated lot developments are only due with express adhesion or a note on the property record (STF Tema 492, STJ Temas 882 and 1183); systematically under-used.
Subsidiary retention request: for contracts before Lei 13.786/2018, the subsidiary request to retain 25% (STJ Súmula 543) is routinely absent when the penalty clause is challenged.
The consumer code as a complementary regime: the CDC applies alongside, not instead of, Lei 9.514/97 and Lei 6.766/79; defences let it displace the special laws.

Reserva Exemplo: Contracts carry a registered fiduciary lien: the preliminary objection of wrong procedure (Lei 9.514/97, arts. 26 and 27) is missing in most defences.
The registration of the lien is treated as constitutive when it is only for publicity: the obligation binds the parties regardless of registration.
No subsidiary request to retain 25% for contracts before Lei 13.786/2018 when the 30% penalty clause is set aside.
Clauses 4.2 and 5.6 are challenged generically, without the individualised rebuttal art. 341 CPC requires.
The distinction between an unmotivated withdrawal and a termination for breach, which changes the retention regime, is not explored.
Parque Modelo: Delay claims: the schedule of infrastructure works is an estimate subject to municipal approvals; the defence lets the contractual date be read as a hard deadline.
The buyer's inertia (no site visit, no building permit request) is not used against presumed lost profits or to apply the duty to mitigate.
The certificate of completion of works (TVO) is not used to argue that the development was legally delivered before physical possession.
Property tax (IPTU) claims: the indemnifiable period and the starting date of interest are never delimited in the alternative.
Vila Fictícia: Association fees: the absence of express adhesion or of a note on the property record is not argued (STF Tema 492, STJ Tema 882).
Association contributions are treated as if they ran with the land (propter rem), an equation to condominium charges the defence does not contest.
Requests to stay the case under STJ Tema 1183 are not renewed on appeal with proper reasoning.
